newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope's doctors say appendix operation a success.
newsitem.headline: Pope's doctors say appendix operation a success.

text.p: Doctors who removed Pope John Paul's appendix on Tuesday said the operation had been a success and the chief surgeon, Francesco Crucitti, said surgery had shown no other serious health problems.
Crucitti announced his verdict to scores of reporters at a special news conference after the Pope, 76, spent about two hours in the operating theatre of Rome's Gemelli hospital for surgery.
Another member of the team of specialists, cardiologist Attilio Maseri, told Reuters: "Everything went okay, perfectly okay (and) very quickly".
Crucitti, reading from a prepared statement, said the Polish-born Pope had shown no problems under anaesthetic during what he called a "textbook appendectomy".

He said the operation, carried out by traditional incision rather than modern keyhole surgery, had confirmed doctors' initial diagnosis that the Pope had been suffering from a recurrent inflammation of the appendix.

He said the operation had "excluded the presence of other pathologies" (problems). The surgery had unleashed widespread speculation that the Pope may have had a tumour, something Crucitti said he excluded "categorically".
